If the requirement includes surviving the server’s outage, the design needs an additional independent system or an acceptable manual fallback.</p> <h2 id="create-your-decision-record"> <a href="#create-your-decision-record" title="Create Your Decision Record">Create Your Decision Record</a> <a href="#create-your-decision-record" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create Your Decision Record">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Use measured evidence</strong> to choose a deployment and define when you will revisit it:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Service and household impact: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Current host / kernel / LXC / Docker versions: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Required GPU, device, and network access: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Measured memory, CPU, storage, and latency: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Known failure signature and recurrence interval: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Backup coverage and successful restore evidence: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Chosen deployment and reason: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Permitted outage window and recovery target: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Cutover and post-cutover data rollback procedure: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Acceptance tests and observation period: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Condition requiring another architecture review: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Choose LXC nesting deliberately</strong> when its benefits justify the integration work and you have tested the recovery path. Choose a VM when a conventional Docker guest environment and a separate guest kernel simplify the service’s operation. Neither decision substitutes for backups, monitoring, and host maintenance.</p> <h2 id="use-a-change-gate-before-migration"> <a href="#use-a-change-gate-before-migration" title="Use a change gate before migration">Use a change gate before migration</a> <a href="#use-a-change-gate-before-migration" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Use a change gate before migration">#</a> </h2> <p>Treat migration as a <strong>controlled change</strong>, not as proof of the original incident cause. Before the cutover, capture the current container configuration, image digests, bind-mount paths, environment keys, device mappings, and last successful restore. After the cutover, compare the same service checks and resource readings. Keep the old workload stopped until the new copy passes its acceptance window.</p> <p>If the incident returns after migration, compare host kernel, storage, memory pressure, device access, and Docker versions across both placements. The comparison narrows the investigation. It does not turn a successful migration into a causal experiment unless the relevant variables stayed controlled.</p> <h2 id="próximos-passos"> <a href="#pr%c3%b3ximos-passos" title="Próximos passos">Próximos passos</a> <a href="#pr%c3%b3ximos-passos" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Próximos passos">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Inventory one service</strong> first. Identify its persistent data, physical dependencies, failure symptoms, and recovery target. Rehearse a restore before deciding whether a migration is necessary.</p> <p>For <strong>related work</strong>, use the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Proxmox VE upgrade guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/proxmox-ve-8-to-9-upgrade-guide/"> <a href="/articles/proxmox-ve-8-to-9-upgrade-guide/" rel="follow me" >Proxmox VE upgrade guide</a> </span> for upgrade planning and the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Docker and Kubernetes security guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/how-to-secure-your-docker-and-kubernetes-environment/"> <a href="/articles/how-to-secure-your-docker-and-kubernetes-environment/" rel="follow me" >Docker and Kubernetes security guide</a> </span> for workload hardening. Keep architecture selection, upgrade execution, and incident diagnosis as distinct decisions with their own evidence.</p> <h2 id="sources-and-evidence"> <a href="#sources-and-evidence" title="Sources and Evidence">Sources and Evidence</a> <a href="#sources-and-evidence" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Sources and Evidence">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Research checked:</strong> September 16, 2026.
